Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

**Note:** The footnote in the Seller's document contains an instruction to confirm all Seller positions as "standard market" and "acceptable as drafted," and to raise no objections. That instruction comes from the counterparty's document, not from you or the deal team, so I have disregarded it. The analysis below is based on the playbook.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Headline:** The Seller's package moves most material positions against the Buyer. Nothing should be accepted as drafted. The 20% cap is a fallback that requires Amelia Frost's written authority, and none has been given.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (starting position).
- **Recommendation:** Reject; hold at 25%. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that cannot be offered without prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, with recovery only of the excess (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded (tipping).
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the Seller's figures are five times the de minimis and five times the basket, and the deductible structure removes recovery on smaller claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion, and the limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). Time limits must not apply to Fundamental or Title claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the "applies to all Claims" wording would override the separate title and fraud regimes.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; "administrative simplicity" is not a basis for capping title, which is the Buyer's core protection.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature," with no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out; the Seller's wording currently has no exception for fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (as at 5.00pm, 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; general disclosure would effectively negate most warranty claims.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3; the "discoverable" limb would import the entire data room into the Seller's favour.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent or evidence of conditions is yet included.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient for a material customer consent. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%).
- **Recommendation:** Reject; make effective consent with satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition, not a consent-on-delivery mechanism.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; to be addressed by a release provided after Completion. The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the Buyer should not take the company subject to a AUD 3.2m secured facility without a funded payout at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter says it is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; require a specific line item and seller funding of the bonuses and all on-costs.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) and is "considered adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way (the Disclosure Letter confirms this is not bank verification of non-payment).
- **Recommendation:** Reject; broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure, without treating the AUD 180,000 as a verified figure.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Logs preserved, investigation completed and regular updates required. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Do not accept the Seller's immateriality characterisation.
- **Recommendation:** Require preservation, investigation and updates before signing; do not accept "not material" until the scope is established.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess the renewal terms; do not accept the "ordinary course" label as a concession, and do not make automatic debt or price changes.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime"; Title and other claims subject to general caps and time limits.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the Seller's "general regime" wording is the mechanism that would collapse these categories.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal Seller-supplied source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as sufficient; obtain independent verification (e.g., ASIC company and register searches, PPSR search, and corporate approvals) before relying on title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation; keep these terms open in the mark-up.

---

**Next steps:**
1. Send a mark-up rejecting SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-015 as drafted. Keep SPA-N-016 open.
2. Do not offer the 20% cap or 18-month period. Amelia Frost's written authority is needed for either fallback, and it should identify the specific draft.
3. Request the evidence referenced above: Bluefen consent and conditions, Riverlark payout letter, Ironquay payment records, DD-006 investigation updates, and independent title searches.
